# Lyapunov structure of the averaged flow {#sec-lyapunov}

The mean and covariance estimates, and the Oja frame, are driven by the *same centred observations*.  This suggests choosing a Lyapunov function whose geometric component is centred at the evolving mean $\mu$, rather than regarding the dependence of $W$ on $\mu$ as an external forcing.  The natural choice is the expected residual of orthogonal projection onto the subspace spanned by $W$.  Its derivative has a useful exact sign along the full averaged flow.

## Mean--covariance dissipation

Let $v=\mu-m$, $Q(\mu)=C+vv^\top$, and $A=\Gamma^{-1}$.  As in @andrieuMoulines2006, equation (52), define

$$
w_{\mathrm{AM}}(\mu,\Gamma)
=\log\det\Gamma+v^\top\Gamma^{-1}v
+\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma^{-1}C).
$$ {#eq-am-energy}

::: {#lem-am-dissipation}
## Exact mean--covariance dissipation

Along @eq-coupled-ode,

$$
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}w_{\mathrm{AM}}(\mu,\Gamma)
=-D_{\mathrm{AM}}(\mu,\Gamma),
$$

where

$$
D_{\mathrm{AM}}
=2v^\top\Gamma^{-1}v+
\big\|\Gamma^{-1/2}(\Gamma-Q(\mu))\Gamma^{-1/2}\big\|_F^2
\geq0.
$$ {#eq-am-dissipation}

Moreover, $D_{\mathrm{AM}}=0$ if and only if $(\mu,\Gamma)=(m,C)$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Differentiate the two parameter coordinates independently.  The identities

$$
\mathrm d(\log\det\Gamma)[U]=\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma^{-1}U),
\qquad
\mathrm d(\Gamma^{-1})[U]=-\Gamma^{-1}U\Gamma^{-1}
$$

give

$$
\nabla_\mu w_{\mathrm{AM}}=2Av,\qquad
\nabla_\Gamma w_{\mathrm{AM}}=A-AQA=A(\Gamma-Q)A.
$$

The corresponding averaged dynamics are $\dot\mu=-v$ and $\dot\Gamma=Q-\Gamma$.  Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot w_{\mathrm{AM}}
&=\langle 2Av,-v\rangle+
  \operatorname{tr}\{A(\Gamma-Q)A(Q-\Gamma)\}\\
&=-2v^\top Av-
  \operatorname{tr}\{A(\Gamma-Q)A(\Gamma-Q)\}.
\end{aligned}
$$

As $A$ is positive definite and $\Gamma-Q$ is symmetric, the trace is
$\|A^{1/2}(\Gamma-Q)A^{1/2}\|_F^2$.  Both nonnegative quantities vanish exactly when $v=0$ and $\Gamma=Q=C$.
:::

## Compactness of the mean--covariance sublevel sets

The coercivity of $w_{\mathrm{AM}}$ will also control the noncompact coordinates of our joint Lyapunov function.

Put $S=C^{-1/2}\Gamma C^{-1/2}\succ0$.  Then

$$
w_{\mathrm{AM}}
=\log\det C+\log\det S
+\operatorname{tr}(S^{-1})
+v^\top\Gamma^{-1}v.
$$ {#eq-am-coercivity-transformation}

Writing $s_1,\ldots,s_d>0$ for the eigenvalues of $S$, the middle terms are
$\sum_i(\log s_i+s_i^{-1})$.  The scalar function $s\mapsto\log s+s^{-1}$ is bounded below by $1$, and tends to $+\infty$ as $s\downarrow0$ or $s\uparrow\infty$.  Consequently, a sublevel bound on $w_{\mathrm{AM}}$ bounds all eigenvalues of $S$ away from $0$ and $\infty$.  The remaining nonnegative quadratic term then bounds $\|v\|$.

In particular, each nonempty sublevel set

$$
K_L=\{(\mu,\Gamma):w_{\mathrm{AM}}(\mu,\Gamma)\leq L\}
$$ {#eq-am-sublevel}

is compact **inside** $\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_{++}^d$, with constants
$0<a_L\leq b_L<\infty$ and $M_L<\infty$ such that

$$
a_LI\preceq\Gamma\preceq b_LI,\qquad
\|\mu-m\|\leq M_L
\qquad \text{on }K_L.
$$ {#eq-compact-eigenvalue-bounds}

The positive lower eigenvalue bound is part of compactness in the *open* positive-definite domain, not a consequence of bounded matrix entries alone.

## The expected reconstruction error

For $W\in\mathrm{St}(d,r)$ write

$$
P_W=I-WW^\top.
$$

This is the orthogonal projector onto the complement of $\operatorname{span}(W)$.  The squared length of the residual after projecting a centred observation $x-\mu$ onto $\operatorname{span}(W)$ is $\|P_W(x-\mu)\|^2$.  Averaging over the common invariant target law gives the natural PCA objective

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal R(\mu,W)
&=\frac12\pi\!\left[\|P_W(X-\mu)\|^2\right]\\
&=\frac12\operatorname{tr}\!\big(P_WQ(\mu)\big)\\
&=\frac12\operatorname{tr}(P_WC)
  +\frac12v^\top P_Wv.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-reconstruction-energy}

The second equality uses @eq-second-moment-identity.  Notice that $\mathcal R\geq0$ and, importantly, the centring parameter $\mu$ is the **same** parameter used in both the covariance and the sample-driven Oja recursions.  This choice connects the objective directly to the algorithm and to classical reconstruction-error Lyapunov arguments for PCA [@plumbley1995].

::: {#lem-reconstruction-gradient}
## The Oja field is the negative reconstruction-error gradient

For fixed $\mu$, the Riemannian gradient on the embedded Stiefel manifold is

$$
\operatorname{grad}_W\mathcal R(\mu,W)
=-P_WQ(\mu)W.
$$ {#eq-reconstruction-gradient}

For fixed $W$, the Euclidean gradient in the mean coordinate is

$$
\nabla_\mu\mathcal R(\mu,W)=P_Wv.
$$ {#eq-reconstruction-mean-gradient}

Hence, along the coupled mean-field system @eq-coupled-ode,

$$
\boxed{
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\mathcal R(\mu,W)
=-\|P_Wv\|^2
-\|P_WQ(\mu)W\|_F^2.
}
$$ {#eq-reconstruction-dissipation}
:::

::: {.proof}
Because $P_W$ is a symmetric idempotent matrix, $v^\top P_Wv=\|P_Wv\|^2$.  Differentiating the last expression in @eq-reconstruction-energy with respect to $\mu$ immediately gives $\nabla_\mu\mathcal R=P_Wv$.

For the $W$ derivative, hold $\mu$ fixed and use
$\operatorname{tr}(P_WQ)=\operatorname{tr}Q-\operatorname{tr}(W^\top QW)$.
The first term does not depend on $W$.  Since $Q$ is symmetric,

$$
\mathrm d_W\mathcal R[U]=-\operatorname{tr}(U^\top QW)
=-\langle QW,U\rangle_F.
$$

Thus the ambient Euclidean gradient is $-QW$.  Its orthogonal projection onto the Stiefel tangent space is

$$
-QW+W\,\operatorname{sym}(W^\top QW)
=-(I-WW^\top)QW=-P_WQW,
$$

where $\operatorname{sym}(W^\top QW)=W^\top QW$ by symmetry of $Q$.

Finally, the first and third components of @eq-coupled-ode are

$$
\dot\mu=-v,\qquad
\dot W=P_WQ(\mu)W=-\operatorname{grad}_W\mathcal R.
$$

Apply the chain rule on $\mathbb R^d\times\mathrm{St}(d,r)$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dot{\mathcal R}
&=\langle P_Wv,-v\rangle
  +\langle-P_WQW,P_WQW\rangle_F\\
&=-\|P_Wv\|^2-\|P_WQW\|_F^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The first negative square is the contribution of the evolving mean; the second is the dissipation generated by the Oja step.
:::

## A Lyapunov function for the full coupled system

::: {#prp-composite}
## Global joint Lyapunov dissipation

For every $\lambda>0$ define

$$
\mathcal L_\lambda(\mu,\Gamma,W)
=w_{\mathrm{AM}}(\mu,\Gamma)+\lambda\mathcal R(\mu,W).
$$ {#eq-composite-energy}

Along every solution of @eq-coupled-ode in
$\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb S_{++}^d\times\mathrm{St}(d,r)$,

$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\dot{\mathcal L}_\lambda
={}&-D_{\mathrm{AM}}(\mu,\Gamma)\\
&-\lambda\|P_W(\mu-m)\|^2\\
&-\lambda\|P_WQ(\mu)W\|_F^2
\leq0.
\end{aligned}
}
$$ {#eq-composite-dissipation}

Equality holds precisely on

$$
\mathcal E=\{(m,C,W):
             (I-WW^\top)CW=0\}.
$$ {#eq-full-equilibria}

Every nonempty sublevel set of $\mathcal L_\lambda$ is compact and forward invariant under @eq-coupled-ode.
:::

::: {.proof}
Add the identities @eq-am-dissipation and @eq-reconstruction-dissipation; there is no unspecified remainder.  All three terms on the right-hand side are nonpositive for every $\lambda>0$.

If $\dot{\mathcal L}_\lambda=0$, then $D_{\mathrm{AM}}=0$, so $\mu=m$ and $\Gamma=C$ by @lem-am-dissipation.  It follows that $Q(\mu)=C$.  The final square vanishes exactly when $P_WCW=0$.  Conversely every such point makes all three terms vanish.

For compactness, $\mathcal R\geq0$ implies

$$
\{\mathcal L_\lambda\leq L\}
\subseteq K_L\times\mathrm{St}(d,r).
$$

The right-hand side is compact by @eq-am-sublevel and compactness of the Stiefel manifold.  The left-hand side is closed there by continuity of $\mathcal L_\lambda$, hence compact.  The derivative inequality shows that its value cannot increase along an ODE solution; therefore the sublevel set is forward invariant.
:::

The proposition is **global for the averaged ODE**: its sign does not depend on restricting the drift calculation to a compact set.  This does not, by itself, establish pathwise boundedness of the *stochastic* recursion.  Uniform kernel and Poisson estimates, and stochastic stability or reinitialization, remain necessary for an unconditional stochastic convergence theorem.

## Equilibria and Lyapunov values

The condition $P_WCW=0$ is equivalent to

$$
CW=WW^\top CW.
$$ {#eq-invariant-subspace}

Thus $\operatorname{span}(W)$ is an invariant $r$-dimensional subspace of the symmetric matrix $C$.  The equilibrium set need not select the leading subspace.

For later use, observe that at a joint equilibrium,

$$
\mathcal L_\lambda(m,C,W)
=\log\det C+d+
  \frac{\lambda}{2}
   \big(\operatorname{tr}C-\operatorname{tr}(W^\top CW)\big).
$$ {#eq-equilibrium-lyapunov-value}

The trace $\operatorname{tr}(W^\top CW)$ is a sum of $r$ eigenvalues of $C$, counted with multiplicity.  Hence $\mathcal L_\lambda$ assumes only **finitely many distinct values** on $\mathcal E$, even when eigenspaces have multiplicity and contain infinitely many possible frames.  This property will allow us to apply the internally chain-transitive limit-set argument of @benaim1999.
